old: When you have a good idea of what’s important to you, you can look at how a group actually functions, not just its public face. Find out how it handled its last conflict, and who can block a decision. How did leaving go for the last person who left? Who owns the land? Then make a choice whether or not it functions in a way that is important to you. It’ll be an uncomfortable conversation, but the view will still be there after you’ve had it.
new: Once you know what matters to you, look past what the group says about itself to how it really works. A recent conflict is a good place to start: how did that get handled? There’s also who can block a decision, and what happened to the last person who left. (And who owns the land!) Then it comes down to whether that’s how you want to live. These are uncomfortable conversations, I know, but the view isn’t going anywhere!
